beats.t: The drop wasn't alone. Two, three, ten. Rain began falling beneath the eclipsed sky.
This isn't me. I haven't done anything.
It is you, my lady. Look at your palm.
Seo Hanbi looked down. The droplets weren't falling from her palm. They rose from it into the sky, then fell again.
That water isn't Black Moon's gift. It's yours by nature. In Four Pillars terms, Gye Water. Rainwater.
My water always drowned people. In the library, it drowned her too.
The ring made you use it that way. Without the ring, it's falling as it was meant to.
Rain poured into Rahu's open mouth. The head choked and stopped. The starlight it had tried to swallow grew heavy with water.
What is this lukewarm thing?
Rahu coughed. Handfuls of starlight spilled from its mouth. The extinguished Bharani began to glow faintly again.
My moon! It's back!
Black smoke settled on Yeoni's notebook. Soaked by rain, it became words again: Grocery shopping. Submit assignment. Go to the sea. A little blurred, but readable.
The trip to the sea survived!
You said you hadn't even set a date.
Exactly why it has to survive. Promises without dates taste best, right? Then I'll set a date and make it taste awful.
Rahu shook its bodiless head. The rain thickened, pushing it backward. The black circle in the sky shrank little by little.
But the rain soon weakened. The stream rising from Seo Hanbi's palm thinned to a thread. Rahu opened its mouth again.
She doesn't have enough water. This rain began with a single drop.
(Bharani. The star that bears. Hold it, then send it out.)
Yeoni cupped their hands toward the sky. Rainwater pooled in their palms. Instead of running off, it swelled within their hands.
You called me a vessel. Then this is how I'll use it. Gather what I receive, then send it back out.
The water stretched upward like a vine and wound around Seo Hanbi's thin stream. As the two twisted into one, the rain strengthened.
You're taking my rain and giving it back?
Half each. That's how it works.
A thing without a ring dares...
Because I have no ring. Your arithmetic doesn't work on me anymore.
Rain spread across all twenty-seven lunar mansions: over roof tiles, into wells, into cracks in stone. It wasn't cold. It was mild, like rain at summer's end.
This rain isn't shriveling my whiskers. Weird rain.
Good rain is like that. Welcome rain, they call it. Rain that falls where it's been awaited.
Something cracked at Yeoni's wrist. The sound of breaking ice. The panel of characters appeared by itself.
[ Year: Im Water · Thawing ]
The frozen Im character in the leftmost column melted. Its black, hardened form returned to clear blue. Warmth spread to Yeoni's fingertips.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ] 8/8
Warm. Not my wrist. Inside.
The water flows now. Gyeong gives birth to Im, and Im nourishes Eul. Officer and Resource in Mutual Generation. Instead of cutting Wood, Metal nourishes it through Water.
Translation, please.
The power Mr. Cat once hurt you with now nourishes you through the rain. Your compatibility has improved enormously.
Compatibility later.
Neo raised his arm. It was still transparent to the shoulder. But the grimace that had accompanied every movement was gone. Cautiously, he flexed his fingers once more.
Neo. Doesn't it hurt anymore?
The pain is less.
The pain? Then what isn't less?
Wet clothes sticking to me.
At Yeoni's suspicious look, Neo turned away and shook his sleeve. Droplets passed through his transparent arm. From Yeoni's side, the wet fabric hid it.
The rain eased. Then Seo Hanbi dropped to her knees. Her face was white as paper. The water rising from her palm had stopped.
Hey! What's wrong?!
I think I used all the water I had left. It's all right. There was only one drop to begin with.
How is that all right?! You're the color of tofu!
Moka dried Seo Hanbi's hair with his apron. Roughly, but thoroughly. She stayed still, as though no one had dried her hair in a very long time.
Moka, you have a heavy hand.
Chef's hands. They're spicy. I've been chopping chilies.
Seo Hanbi reached into her coat's inner pocket. Not for the soaked ledger. For a little folded note with a drumstick-shaped knot at its end.
This is what I must return first. The only thing I didn't enter in the ledger. I couldn't.
Yeoni took the note and untied the knot. A name was written in clumsy handwriting. The child's own hand.
Dodam.
The instant the name was spoken, a drum sounded far away. Boom. Boom. A clumsy, excited rhythm. From the sky toward the Island of Companions.
I hear it. A drum. That rhythm's such a mess, it has to be the kid.
Dodam. Right. It was Dodam. How did I forget?
Because I took it. When you take a name, others forget the child too. That's why the applause stopped.
I know. I saw the child drop the drumsticks that day. You smiled then.
I did. Because a line in my ledger balanced. That smile was mine too. Not Black Moon's.
Yeoni bit their lip. Moka turned away. No one took Seo Hanbi's side. She didn't look as though she expected anyone to.
But I carried the name inside my cloak. Whenever I tried to erase it, the ledger got wet.
This time, Seo Hanbi opened the ledger. One line in the collection column: Dodam's applause. Wet with rain, it slowly blurred. The letters dissolved and ran away with the water.
It's moving. It wouldn't budge before.
I thought rain couldn't release what rain hadn't collected. But returning the name first seems to have shown the ledger a way.
Then do them one at a time. One line whenever it rains. The market grandmothers. The underground-stage children. The people of the time island.
How many times will it have to rain before it's all repaid?
Many. Very many.
Then we could start selling umbrellas.
Yeoni wiped their tears with a sleeve and tucked the note into the notebook's first page. Then they looked straight at Seo Hanbi.
Come with us. But you're on trial.
On trial?
I'll keep watching. To see whether you really return them, one by one. Once you've returned everything, I'll consider it. Forgiveness.
Probation, then.
Yes. In ledger terms: outstanding.
Outstanding. The word I wrote most in my ledger, now applied to me.
I'll watch too. My eyes still work fine.
Me too. To monitor you, I'll need your birth date and—
I told you, that's a debt.
Someone cure this man's compatibility obsession!
Laughter burst out. It rang around the well after the rain like a sound heard for the first time. Seo Hanbi didn't laugh. She pressed her lips together, holding back tears.
Behind the well, a little apart from the others, Yundal pulled his glove on and crouched beside Neo. The hole in his palm had grown large enough to show through it.
Neo. Water passed straight through your arm earlier.
You saw?
Only me. My lady was busy picking up cards.
Then that promise still stands?
If they forget me, remember me. Yes. It stands. I'm usually the one forgotten, so remembering is new for me.
It's a heavy thing to leave you carrying alone. Don't joke it away.
That's why you're leaving it with a con artist. A real fortune-teller wouldn't take this contract. It's a loss.
Neo didn't answer. He watched Yeoni for a long time. They were wringing out Seo Hanbi's wet coat and scolding her.
Then the sky split. The eclipse tore open, spilling enormous sheets of paper through the gap. Cards. Each as large as a door.
Rahu's head was drawn between the cards. Ketu's tail followed. Both seeped into the illustrations and became shadows.
I will wait beyond the twenty-two cards. In the next sky, neither your umbrella nor your rain will help.
And that cat. Half mine already. Count the threads.
Yeoni looked at their wrist. The red thread leading to Neo. At some point, two strands had become one. Even that last strand was fraying.
Neo. The thread.
I know.
Don't end with 'I know.' Tell me properly this time.
When we reach the next sky, I'll tell you. I promise.
A card fell at Yeoni's feet, face down. A dark blue back patterned with stars. They tried to turn it over, but it wouldn't move, as though glued to the floor.
Your birth card, my lady. When the time comes, it will turn over by itself.
(When is that? Everyone says later. There are too many laters.)
The last raindrop fell. Footprints marked the wet stone: Yeoni's, Seo Hanbi's, Moka's, Yundal's.
Only where Neo had walked were there no footprints. Yeoni couldn't take their eyes from the card.
